maturity: Pre-validation release (Beta or Provisional), L2 GCOV product version 1.0.2

method.speckle_filter: 4x4 multilook in linear power (40 m pixels)
method.notes: Water = HH and HV both below threshold. Thresholds from the valley of the during-scene histogram. New flood = water(during) and not water(before). Pixel area counted only where both dates have data. Permanent open water has the same brightness in both dates (HH -18.4 vs -17.7 dB) while land is about 3 dB brighter on 17 Jan, so one absolute threshold is used. Moving the 5 Jan thresholds by the land-peak difference gives a higher estimate; both are reported.

context_figures.source: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio #5661, NISAR Reveals Major Flooding in Mozambique

limitations: NISAR data are provisional and may be reprocessed.
The first scene (5 Jan) was taken when flooding may already have started in places, so 'new water' means new compared with that date.
Flooded forest and crops can look bright to the radar and are probably missed by a darkness threshold.
Rough water (wind) and relief shadows can cause errors. Thresholds were set on one scene and not validated against an independent map yet.
